question: m09
q: Have building approvals picked up since the RBA started cutting?

transcript.answer:
**Yes, approvals are higher than before the cuts, though the pickup has been modest and it has continued through the 2026 rate rises. Houses account for most of it.**

**Rate path (RBA cash rate, monthly average)**
- The rate was 4.35% through January 2025.
- The cuts came in February, May and August 2025, taking it to 3.60% by September 2025.
- It was then raised through 2026. It was 3.83% in February and 4.35% by June 2026, and it was 4.36% in September 2026.

**Total residential dwelling approvals, Australia (ABS, original series, dwelling units)**

| Period | Approvals |
|---|---|
| Aug 2024 – Jan 2025 (before cuts) | 91,287 |
| Feb – Jul 2025 (first six months of cuts) | 98,285 (+7.7%) |
| Aug 2025 – Jan 2026 (rate at 3.60%) | 95,992 (+5.2% vs pre-cuts) |
| Feb – Jul 2026 (rate rising) | 110,563 (+12.5% vs Feb – Jul 2025) |
| Jan – Aug 2026 vs Jan – Aug 2025 | 138,226 vs 126,983 (+8.9%) |

- The latest month, August 2026, was 16,967 approvals. That is up 10% on August 2025 (15,377) but down from 19,273 in July 2026.
- Monthly figures are noisy. Three of the four 2026 months from February to May were around 17,200–19,200. June and July were about 19,100–19,300.

**Houses versus everything else**
- **Houses:** January to August 2026 had 84,534 approvals, against 74,108 a year earlier (+14%). August 2026 was 11,134, up from 9,730 in August 2025.
- **Other dwellings (townhouses and apartments):** these are my estimate, calculated as total minus houses. They were about 53,700 in January to August 2026 against about 52,900 a year earlier (+1.5%). That is essentially flat.

**Caveats**
- Only the original (not seasonally adjusted) series was available to me, so I compared like periods with like.
- Approvals kept rising after the RBA started hiking in February 2026. Approvals reflect decisions made earlier, and rates alone probably don't explain the rise. Other factors such as housing supply policy, construction costs and demand could also be at work. The data here can't separate them.
